 IRS names ten members to electronic tax advisory committee
 ETAAC advises on digital tax administration and supports efforts to combat identity theft and refund fraud.
 Ellichipuram Umesh 
 November 16, 2026 
 Share
 Copy Link 
 Share on X 
 Share on Linkedin 
 Share on Facebook 
 ETAAC members collaborate with the Security Summit, an alliance of the IRS. Credit: Lane V. Erickson/Shutterstock.com. 
 The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) has appointed ten new members to its Electronic Tax Administration Advisory Committee (ETAAC).
 ETAAC is a public forum for discussion of electronic tax administration. Its members also work with the Security Summit, which brings together the IRS, state tax administrators, and the tax industry to address identity theft and refund fraud.

 The new members include Shelly Abril, head of payroll product compliance at Gusto. She oversees compliance for a platform that processes payroll taxes for more than 500,000 small and mid-sized businesses.
 Jack Hyre, president of THG & Associates, has experience in small business tax strategy, corporate restructuring, and operational finance.
 Mindy Mayo is a managing director in KPMG’s Silicon Valley office. She has more than 30 years of experience in employment tax and has advised clients on payroll matters during different stages of the company lifecycle.
 Christopher Modi brings experience in strategic innovation, systems management, fintech software development, and cybersecurity. His background also includes artificial intelligence, robotic process automation, blockchain, and data analytics.
 Richard Phipps is vice-president and tax compliance officer at Fidelity Investments. His experience includes tax governance, regulatory compliance, and operational risk management at global financial institutions.
 Yehuda Tenenbaum founded Y10 Tax Solutions in 2019. As an enrolled agent, he advises W-2 employees, self-employed professionals, small business owners, real estate investors, retirees, and public safety officers.
 Kathryn Tracy is an enrolled agent and former IRS revenue agent. She has owned and operated an accounting and income tax return preparation business since 1992.
 Michelle Potter Trevena is a principal in Ryan’s Employment Tax Practice. The practice provides federal, state, local, and international tax services across multiple jurisdictions.
 John Valentine has led the Utah State Tax Commission for 12 years. Before taking up the role, he spent 38 years in private practice as a tax attorney, focusing mainly on federal and state tax matters.
 Amanda Watson is an enrolled agent and customer success professional at Taxwell, also known as Drake Software. She has more than 21 years of experience in the tax software sector.
 IRS CEO Frank Bisignano said: “ETAAC provides a great venue for tax professionals to provide the IRS with feedback on electronic tax administration. “The members of the committee bring vast amounts of invaluable real-world experience and insight to the IRS and help improve the tax system for all taxpayers.”
